name: almach
archetype: Directional maker on crypto Up/Down windows (two-wallet cluster with bosona)
headline: bosona's twin: the same market mix, price distribution and maker style, with 6,524 shared transactions. Real and persistent profit with little rebate dependence, but no public-data rule matches its fills and every public-data maker version loses in the same windows.
mechanism: 92% of sampled fills are maker fills (on-chain, 95% CI 87-95%) across BTC 5m (53%), 15m (30%), hourly and 4h Up/Down windows. Directional residual +$83.5k with a 58% win rate; locked pair spread -$23.0k. Shares bought at 0.35 win 40% of the time.

match.detail: directional maker: held-out AUC 0.476 (perm p=0.74) on BTC 5m, 0.457 (p=0.79) on BTC 15m; spot-latency taker: AUC 0.50 (p=0.70)

backtest.detail: public-data maker on held-out windows: -17.7% (5m), -23.9% (15m), -14% to -18% with optimistic at-touch fills; almach's own maker fills +10.3% on 15m (p=0.30); the fitted taker rule +7.7% at 0 s (p=0.23) fades to +0.9% at 10 s

replicable.detail: slow makers are adversely selected at every latency tested; the edge needs queue priority and fast cancels

persistence.detail: last 30 days significant (p=0.003), no decline (p=0.30); ~18% taker rebate, at 0% tier ~$70k/month

reasons: No public-data rule reproduces its fills (held-out AUC at chance on 5m and 15m).
Every public-data maker version loses significantly in the same windows, even under first-in-queue fills.
Appears to be the same operator as bosona.
